text: 2 x 2 factorial design whereby message content and framing served as the independent variables, as shown in the table below. The local and general content priming factors were an estimated additional number of employees needed by each company versus the overall percentage of additional workers needed across the industry, respectively. The quality of building performance work versus the societal and homeowner benefits from energy efficiency provided the content framing. The dependent variable was the number of employees contractors think they will have in 5 years. Table A-4. 2 x 2 Messaging Experiment Quality Framing Energy Efficiency Framing Local Prime Local + Quality Local + Energy Efficiency General Prime General + Quality General + Energy Efficiency These following four prompts, representing each combination of priming and framing, were randomly assigned to survey participants, with each participant receiving only one of them. A question on the number of workers currently employed at each firm was asked earlier in the survey, providing a baseline to which the researchers could compare and determine the extent to which contractors expect their firm’s employment to change. • Local + Quality: One million workers will be needed for residential buildings across the United States by 2035. This would mean that nearly every company would need to hire at least one more employee. High-quality work will be essential to ensuring that these improvements meet homeowner expectations and last for years to come. Given this unprecedented demand, how many employees do you think will work at your company in 5 years? • Local + Energy Efficiency: One million workers will be needed for residential buildings across the United States by 2035. This would mean that nearly every company would need to hire at least one more employee. The shift to electrification and improved energy efficiency will play a crucial role in reducing carbon emissions and lowering utility costs for homeowners.
